A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PSI framework and experiments. Text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable, including the new Appendix D in v2; no material gaps prevent comparison.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix B report original real-world manipulation experiments, simulated robot-embodiment comparisons, and demonstration-scaling results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and additionally reports a measured simulation runtime in Appendix D.

M1.justification: The perception pipelines, simulated grasp-trajectory filtering, policy architecture, losses, two-stage training, and nearest-anchor grasp selection remain unchanged. Explicitly identifying eight anchors and dataset-specific training stages clarifies the existing procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same HOI4D pretraining data, four manipulation tasks, and four robot embodiments. The added runtime analysis does not introduce another dataset, task, or deployment scenario.

E2.justification: Tables 1–3 retain the same filtering/grasping ablations, General-Flow comparator, and ImageNet/R3M pretraining comparisons. Track2Act and EgoMimic receive additional discussion in v2 but are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix D adds average simulation time per grasp-trajectory pair as an evaluation metric. Existing task-success criteria, splits, training budgets, and evaluation counts remain unchanged. The newly stated xArm7-based validation filtering documents an existing evaluation rather than establishing a changed protocol.

E4.justification: v2 adds simulation-runtime analysis and qualitatively reports that densifying the eight-anchor grid does not significantly improve grasp selection, without providing a quantitative sensitivity comparison. Existing filtering, grasping, failure-visualization, and data-scaling analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports across-seed variability, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests. The new runtime mean has no accompanying repetition count or uncertainty estimate; the explicit mention of 20 evaluation episodes restates counts already visible in v1's tables.

E6.justification: All 80 success-count entries in Tables 1–5 remain unchanged. Appendix D newly reports 9.68 seconds per simulated grasp-trajectory pair and estimates 121 seconds for 50 demonstrations and eight anchors with 32 threads. v2 also adds the qualitative finding that denser anchors offer little benefit.

T1.justification: The pose representation, mathematical definitions, losses, and rigid-attachment assumption are retained. No theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical derivation is added; Appendix D provides a straightforward runtime calculation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: simulation-filtered human-video imitation, task-compatible grasp selection, and sample-efficient manipulation without robot demonstrations. The added details do not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 newly explains ICP's drawing failures through the marker's small point cloud and emphasizes how filtering reduces the gap from FoundationPose. v2 also explains the efficiency rationale for anchor approximation and simulation. The rigid-object and closed-loop visual-domain limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly documents shared HOI4D-pretrained initialization, simulated robot-base placement, and xArm7-feasibility filtering of validation trajectories. Architecture and optimizer details move from Section 4.1 to Appendix C with their settings preserved.

R1.justification: v2 adds the NVIDIA Isaac Sim reference and discusses PSI's data-collection costs relative to already-cited Track2Act and EgoMimic. Section 2 also clarifies how image-translation approaches support reinforcement-learning rewards. The overall research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized explanatory edits, standardizes citation formatting, updates affiliations and publication information, and adds descriptive subheadings in Appendix C. Moving implementation details and adding Appendix D modestly reorganizes the document without extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: The eight figures and five tables retain their substantive content and designs. Publication headers, a reformatted affiliation block, and text reflow alter layout; Table 5 moves from page 16 to page 17. There is no substantial visual redesign.

improvement.justification: v2 improves transparency by specifying pretraining initialization and validation filtering, explaining ICP's drawing failures, and adding measured simulation-cost evidence. These are useful, limited gains over v1. The core performance evidence remains unchanged, while missing timing hardware/repetition details and quantitative anchor-density results limit the strength of the additions.
